Event_title: Middlesbrough, Scarborough, Halifax & Hull: Using the Registers of Deeds to evidence women’s capital investment in 19th century Yorkshire
Description: The Yorkshire Registers of Deeds, which date from the early 1700s until the 1970s, contain thousands of peoples’ names linked to property transactions across all three Ridings of the county. As such, they are an amazing resource for genealogists and local historians, but sadly underused because of their relative inaccessibility. My presentation will give a brief introduction to the Registers, highlighting the type of information available about people and places, families and inheritance, before focusing on their importance when researching women’s lives. The latter half of the presentation will reveal the significance of women’s capital investment in the growth of four Yorkshire towns in the late 1880s – Middlesbrough, Scarborough, Halifax & Hull – and challenge the perception that land ownership and property investment are often perceived as particularly male activities. Although the formal organisational lending sector was expanding during this period, the majority of mortgage documentation relates to peer-to-peer lending, the impact of which is missing entirely from published research.
